symptoms.name: No visible symptoms
symptoms.description: Leaf looks uniformly green with no spots, coatings or deformation.

symptoms.name: Yellowing (chlorosis)
symptoms.description: Leaf or parts of it turn pale or yellow.

symptoms.name: Spots with yellow halo
symptoms.description: Spots surrounded by a yellow ring of tissue.

symptoms.name: Brown spots / lesions
symptoms.description: Distinct brown, dead (necrotic) spots on the leaf blade.

symptoms.name: Dark or black spots
symptoms.description: Very dark brown to black spots or lesions.

symptoms.name: Concentric rings (target spots)
symptoms.description: Lesions with rings inside them, like a target or bull's-eye.

symptoms.name: Many small spots / speckling
symptoms.description: Numerous tiny spots scattered over the leaf.

symptoms.name: Water-soaked lesions
symptoms.description: Greasy, dark-green or translucent patches that look wet.

symptoms.name: Olive-green velvety lesions
symptoms.description: Olive to dark-green patches with a velvety or sooty surface.

symptoms.name: Orange / rust-coloured pustules
symptoms.description: Raised orange, brown or cinnamon powdery pustules or spots.

symptoms.name: White powdery coating
symptoms.description: White to grey powder on the leaf surface that can be rubbed off.

symptoms.name: Fuzzy mould growth
symptoms.description: Velvety or downy grey, olive or white growth, usually on the leaf underside.

symptoms.name: Long / rectangular lesions
symptoms.description: Lesions that are long and narrow (cigar-shaped) or limited by veins into rectangles.

symptoms.name: Leaf curling / cupping
symptoms.description: Leaves curl upward or downward, cup, or roll.

symptoms.name: Mosaic / mottling
symptoms.description: Patchwork of light-green or yellow and dark-green areas.

symptoms.name: Leaf distortion / small leaves
symptoms.description: Leaves are puckered, narrow, fern-like, crinkled or much smaller than normal.

symptoms.name: Blotchy asymmetric mottle
symptoms.description: Irregular yellow blotches that do not mirror each other across the midrib.

symptoms.name: Interveinal stripes (tiger stripes)
symptoms.description: Yellow or red-brown bands between the veins with green tissue along the veins.

symptoms.name: Stippling / bronzing
symptoms.description: Fine pale dots that merge into a dull bronze or greyish look.

symptoms.name: Fine webbing
symptoms.description: Silky webbing on the leaf, usually on the underside.

symptoms.name: Edge / margin browning
symptoms.description: Browning or scorching that starts at the leaf margin or tip.

symptoms.name: Large dead (blighted) areas
symptoms.description: Big brown or black dead areas covering a large part of the leaf.

symptoms.name: Shot holes
symptoms.description: Small holes where dead spot centres have dropped out.

symptoms.name: Purple / red spot margins
symptoms.description: Spots with purple, reddish or dark-red borders.

symptoms.name: Vein yellowing / vein clearing
symptoms.description: Veins turn yellow or clear while the tissue between them stays green.

diseases.name: Apple scab
diseases.management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves, prune for air flow, plant scab-resistant varieties.

diseases.name: Black rot (frog-eye leaf spot)
diseases.management: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood / cankers, prune infected branches.

diseases.name: Apple rust (cedar apple rust)
diseases.management: Remove nearby juniper / cedar hosts where possible; plant resistant varieties.

diseases.name: Alternaria leaf spot / blotch
diseases.model_class: AppleLeaf9 Alternaria leaf spot + Kashmir Alternaria
diseases.management: Collect and destroy fallen leaves, prune for air flow and light, avoid excess nitrogen, keep orchard floor weed-free.

diseases.name: Marssonina leaf blotch (brown spot)
diseases.management: Collect and destroy fallen leaves in autumn, prune for air flow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness; it causes early leaf fall in rainy summers.

diseases.name: Grey leaf spot
diseases.management: Remove fallen leaves, improve air flow; usually controlled by the routine orchard spray programme.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.management: Prune out white (infected) shoots and buds in winter and spring, keep the canopy open.

diseases.name: Apple mosaic
diseases.pathogen: Apple mosaic virus (ApMV; spread by grafting with infected budwood)
diseases.management: No cure. Use certified virus-free rootstocks and budwood; keep tree vigour with balanced nutrition.

diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Common rust

diseases.name: Northern / Turcicum leaf blight
diseases.management: Grow resistant hybrids, rotate crops, plough under infected residue.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Black rot

diseases.management: Prune in dry weather, protect large pruning wounds, remove dead arms and badly infected vines.

diseases.name: Leaf blight (Isariopsis leaf spot)
diseases.management: Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves; keep the canopy open.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (spread by the Asian citrus psyllid)
diseases.management: Use certified disease-free nursery plants, control psyllids, remove confirmed infected trees.

diseases.name: Bacterial spot
diseases.management: Use disease-free seed and transplants, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate 2–3 years away from pepper/tomato.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.management: Remove lower infected leaves, keep plants well nourished, rotate crops, avoid late-evening irrigation.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.management: Act immediately — spreads within days in cool wet weather. Remove infected plants, use healthy seed tubers, earth up tubers, contact KVK for a spray schedule.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly, especially in cool humid weather (late blight risk).

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.management: Grow tolerant varieties, space plants for air flow, remove heavily infected old leaves.

diseases.name: Bacterial spot
diseases.pathogen: Xanthomonas spp. (X. vesicatoria, X. euvesicatoria, X. perforans, X. gardneri)
diseases.management: Use clean seed and transplants, avoid working with wet plants, rotate away from tomato/pepper.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.management: Remove lower infected leaves, mulch to stop soil splash, stake plants, rotate crops.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.management: Act immediately. Remove and destroy infected plants, avoid overhead irrigation, contact KVK for a spray schedule.

diseases.name: Leaf mould
diseases.management: Reduce humidity (ventilate polyhouses), avoid wetting leaves, remove infected leaves.

diseases.name: Septoria leaf spot
diseases.management: Remove lower infected leaves, mulch, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops.

diseases.name: Two-spotted spider mite damage
plantdoc: Tomato two spotted spider mites leaf
diseases.management: Spray water on the leaf underside, remove heavily infested leaves, conserve predatory mites, avoid dusty field edges.

diseases.name: Target spot
diseases.management: Remove lower leaves and crop debris, improve air flow, rotate crops.

diseases.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
diseases.pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (begomovirus, spread by whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
diseases.management: Use resistant hybrids and nets in the nursery, control whiteflies, uproot infected plants early.

diseases.name: Tomato mosaic virus
diseases.pathogen: Tomato mosaic virus (tobamovirus, spread by contact and seed)
diseases.management: Use certified seed, wash hands and tools (milk or soap) when handling plants, remove infected plants.

diseases.name: Healthy
diseases.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring weekly.

diseases.name: Blast
diseases.management: Avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties, keep bunds weed-free.

diseases.name: Brown spot
diseases.management: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies (often potassium / silicon), use treated healthy seed.

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf blight
diseases.management: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, drain field water from infected plots.

diseases.name: Brown (leaf) rust
diseases.management: Grow resistant varieties recommended for your zone; sow on time.

diseases.name: Yellow (stripe) rust
diseases.management: Grow resistant varieties, report early patches to the agriculture department.

diseases.name: Cotton leaf curl disease
diseases.pathogen: Cotton leaf curl begomoviruses (spread by whitefly)
diseases.management: Grow tolerant hybrids, control whiteflies, remove weed hosts and infected plants.

diseases.name: Chilli leaf curl
diseases.pathogen: Chilli leaf curl begomoviruses (whitefly); thrips / mites cause similar curl
diseases.management: Raise seedlings under insect net, control whiteflies and thrips, uproot infected plants.

diseases.name: Cercospora / anthracnose leaf spot
diseases.management: Use healthy seed, remove infected leaves and fruit, rotate crops.

diseases.name: Yellow vein mosaic
diseases.pathogen: Bhendi yellow vein mosaic virus (begomovirus, whitefly)
diseases.management: Grow resistant varieties, control whiteflies, uproot infected plants early.

diseases.name: Sigatoka leaf spot
diseases.management: Remove and destroy infected leaves, improve drainage, avoid dense planting.

diseases.name: Tikka (early / late leaf spot)
diseases.management: Rotate crops, remove volunteer plants and crop residue.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.management: Prune for air flow; monitor closely during flowering in cool, cloudy weather.

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.management: Prune and destroy infected twigs and leaves, avoid overhead irrigation.

diseases.name: Citrus canker
diseases.management: Prune infected twigs in dry weather, use windbreaks, use disease-free nursery plants.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.management: Wide spacing, drip instead of overhead irrigation, remove infected leaves.

diseases.name: Little leaf
diseases.management: Uproot infected plants early, control leafhoppers, remove weed hosts.

diseases.name: Purple blotch
diseases.management: Rotate crops, avoid dense planting, remove infected leaves.

diseases.name: Alternaria blight
diseases.management: Sow on time, use healthy seed, remove lower infected leaves.

diseases.name: Papaya ringspot
diseases.management: Raise seedlings under net, grow a barrier crop, remove infected plants early.

diseases.name: Nutrient deficiency (non-infectious)
diseases.pathogen: Not a pathogen — nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, iron or zinc imbalance
diseases.management: Get a soil test (Soil Health Card) before adding any fertiliser.

visual_pattern_check.name: Whole-plant symptom pattern check
visual_pattern_check.procedure: Walk the field and check where symptoms appear (old vs young leaves, lower vs upper canopy, scattered plants vs patches), whether fruits or stems are affected, and how fast it is spreading.
visual_pattern_check.confirms: Helps separate infectious diseases (spreading, patchy) from nutrient, herbicide or weather damage (uniform, follows rows or sprays).

hand_lens_spores.name: Hand-lens (10–20x) check of lesions
hand_lens_spores.procedure: Look at lesion centres and the leaf underside with a 10–20x hand lens for spores, powdery growth, pustules, black fruiting bodies (dots) or mites.
hand_lens_spores.confirms: Fungal structures (pustules, fruiting bodies, mould) point to a fungal disease; moving dots point to mites.

moist_chamber.name: Moist-chamber (humid box) incubation
moist_chamber.procedure: Place a freshly infected leaf on wet tissue paper in a closed plastic box or bag at room temperature, away from sunlight. After 1–3 days inspect the lesions with a hand lens.
moist_chamber.confirms: Fungal or oomycete growth forming on the lesion margins (white downy growth for late blight, dark spores for early blight / leaf spots). No growth after 3 days suggests bacterial, viral or non-infectious causes.

spore_microscopy.name: Microscopic spore identification
spore_microscopy.procedure: Scrape or tape-lift growth from a lesion, mount in lactophenol cotton blue and examine under a compound microscope. Compare spore shape, septation and size with reference descriptions.
spore_microscopy.confirms: Identifies the fungal genus (e.g. Alternaria beaked multi-celled spores, Septoria thread-like spores in pycnidia, Cercospora long needle-like spores).

culture_isolation.name: Pathogen isolation on culture medium
culture_isolation.procedure: Surface-sterilise small pieces from the lesion edge and plate on potato dextrose agar (fungi) or nutrient / King's B agar (bacteria). Identify colonies by morphology, microscopy or sequencing.
culture_isolation.confirms: Isolates and identifies the causal organism; the standard confirmation for fungal and bacterial diseases.

bacterial_ooze.name: Bacterial ooze / streaming test
bacterial_ooze.procedure: Cut a thin piece across the margin of a fresh lesion, place it in a drop of clean water on a glass slide and watch under a microscope (or against light for stems in a glass of water) for milky streams flowing out of the cut edge.
bacterial_ooze.confirms: Streaming of bacteria from the cut tissue indicates a bacterial disease; fungal lesions do not stream.

koh_string_test.name: KOH (3%) string test
koh_string_test.procedure: Mix a loopful of a pure bacterial colony with a drop of 3% potassium hydroxide on a slide and lift the loop slowly.
koh_string_test.confirms: A sticky string forming indicates Gram-negative bacteria (e.g. Xanthomonas, Pseudomonas), supporting a bacterial-spot diagnosis.

pcr_bacteria.name: PCR for bacterial pathogen
pcr_bacteria.procedure: Lab extracts DNA from lesion tissue or a pure culture and runs species-specific PCR (e.g. Xanthomonas spp. for bacterial spot).
pcr_bacteria.confirms: Definitive identification of the bacterial species.

elisa_virus.name: ELISA / lateral-flow immunostrip for virus
elisa_virus.procedure: Grind young symptomatic leaf tissue in extraction buffer and test with a virus-specific immunostrip or DAS-ELISA kit (e.g. Tomato mosaic virus / Tobamovirus).
elisa_virus.confirms: Presence of the specific virus antigen; a negative strip on a strongly symptomatic plant points to a different virus.

pcr_virus.name: PCR / RT-PCR for virus
pcr_virus.procedure: Lab extracts nucleic acid from young leaves and runs PCR (DNA viruses such as begomoviruses, e.g. TYLCV) or RT-PCR (RNA viruses such as tobamoviruses).

vector_check.name: Insect-vector inspection (whitefly / aphid / psyllid)
vector_check.procedure: Shake or tap shoots over white paper and inspect the underside of young leaves; use yellow sticky traps for 2–3 days.
vector_check.confirms: Presence of the vector (whiteflies for leaf-curl begomoviruses, Asian citrus psyllid for greening, aphids for many mosaics) supports, but does not prove, a vector-borne virus/bacterium.

mite_paper_tap.name: White-paper tap test for mites
mite_paper_tap.procedure: Hold white paper under a stippled leaf and tap the leaf sharply. Watch the paper for tiny moving specks; check the leaf underside with a hand lens for mites, eggs and webbing.
mite_paper_tap.confirms: Moving specks and webbing confirm spider mites; no mites suggests another cause of stippling (e.g. ozone, thrips, nutrient).

iodine_starch_test.name: Iodine starch test (citrus greening screen)
iodine_starch_test.procedure: Scratch or cut a symptomatic leaf, rub the cut with an iodine solution (or soak a leaf disc). Compare with a healthy leaf.
iodine_starch_test.confirms: Dark blue-black staining shows starch build-up typical of greening; a screening test only — confirm with qPCR.

qpcr_hlb.name: qPCR for Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus
qpcr_hlb.procedure: Send mature symptomatic leaves with midribs to a citrus lab for quantitative PCR.
qpcr_hlb.confirms: Definitive detection of the greening bacterium.

oomycete_strip.name: Phytophthora lateral-flow / LAMP test
oomycete_strip.procedure: Test lesion-margin tissue with a Phytophthora immunostrip or LAMP assay.
oomycete_strip.confirms: Presence of Phytophthora (late blight); separates it from early blight and bacterial lesions.

underside_growth_check.name: Leaf-underside growth check
underside_growth_check.procedure: Turn affected leaves over early in the morning and look for white, grey, olive or purple downy / velvety growth beneath the spots.
underside_growth_check.confirms: Growth under the lesions points to downy mildew, late blight or leaf mould rather than a bacterial spot.

wood_cross_section.name: Wood cross-section (trunk diseases)
wood_cross_section.procedure: Cut across the cane, spur or trunk from which a symptomatic shoot grows and look for dark spots or streaks in the wood.
wood_cross_section.confirms: Dark streaking or concentric dark spots in the wood support Esca / trunk disease; send wood to a lab for fungal isolation.

soil_and_tissue_test.name: Soil test and leaf nutrient analysis
soil_and_tissue_test.procedure: Collect soil from the root zone and recently matured leaves; send to a Soil Testing Laboratory (Soil Health Card scheme) for nutrient analysis.
soil_and_tissue_test.confirms: Rules out nutrient deficiency or toxicity that can mimic yellowing, mottling and margin scorch.

rub_test_powdery.name: Rub test for powdery mildew
rub_test_powdery.procedure: Rub the white coating gently with a finger or wet cloth.
rub_test_powdery.confirms: Powdery mildew growth rubs off and leaves green or yellowed tissue below; spray residue or dust behaves differently under a hand lens (no threads/chains of spores).

xylem_scorch_check.name: Leaf-scorch vs drought check
xylem_scorch_check.procedure: Check soil moisture at root depth and whether scorch is on individual leaflets with purple spots (disease) or uniform on the whole plant after hot dry days (drought / salt).
xylem_scorch_check.confirms: Separates fungal leaf scorch from water stress and salt injury.
